question: Related Questions Q. I am going to get married soon in-sha-Allah, but I have a doubt about the mahr 2743 views Q. What says Uluma-e-Karam in the light of Quran-o-Sunnah: There is a practice in our area according to which Nikah is done in proper Islamic way at the time of engagement but at the time of rukhsati, again Nikah is done in the same way. Uluma doing so admit the fact that once Nikah is done at the time of engagement, it is not necessary to repeat it at the time of rukhsati however they says it is better to repeat it ( or renew it ) at the time of rukhsati. It is necessary to mention here that it is an integaral part of the marriage ceremony in our area to arrange a function of doing nikah on the evening of Shabe-uroosi in which all close relatives participate. So if this function is not done, there would be confusion in the mind of relatives. My question is: ? whether this practice of repeating nikah is according to Quran-o-Sunnah and is there any evidence available in Sunnah. ? Is there any Hadees proving that this practice is forbidden. ? Then in case there is no evidence available in Sunah regarding allowing or disallowing, whether one can be allowed to repeat nikah for the sake of making people?s mind clear. 3765 views Q. answer: Social Matters >> Nikah (Marriage) Question ID: 45490 Country: India Title: Calling Wife as Mother Question: Some people say that calling your wife amma, maa, in anger is prohibited. What does Shariah say about it? If someone is angry and tells his wife sorry ‘meri maa’ or any other word like this what should he do? Answer ID: 45490 Posted on: Sep 1, 2020 Bismillah hir-Rahman nir-Rahim ! (Fatwa: 871/688/B=1434) It is nonsense to call one’s wife mother or amma. However, if someone said so it shall not have any adverse effect on his nikah. Allah (Subhana Wa Ta'ala) knows Best Darul Ifta, Darul Uloom Deoband, India
